rules.statement: Don't ask for upgrade or rebuild notes about runtime or binary breaks, such as a changed public const value or a newly reserved name that now throws, when the package has never been released and the CHANGELOG already marks the change **Breaking:**.
rules.why: A package that has never shipped has no compiled consumers, so nobody has the old value or behavior to break. The Breaking entry is enough.
rules.check: Before reporting, look at version.json, for example a 0.0.1-alpha pre-release that has never shipped, and at the CHANGELOG entry. Report only if a released version exists or the entry doesn't flag the break.

rules.statement: Don't ask to move a CHANGELOG entry for a security hardening change, such as host-only cookies or form-POST logout, into `### Changed`. Hardening changes belong under `### Security`, with **Breaking:** on each one that breaks callers.
rules.why: Hardening changes are filed in the Security group, and the Breaking flag on each entry already makes the break visible.
rules.check: Check which heading the entry actually sits under in the [Unreleased] section and whether it is flagged **Breaking:** before reporting misfiled entries.

rules.statement: Don't report a plain-http localhost origin in a Development-only CORS allow-list when the dev tool that serves that origin can't serve HTTPS, such as `vite preview`.
rules.why: The preview server only serves plain http, so the origin is kept on purpose. It appears only in the Development configuration.
rules.check: Check that the entry is only in appsettings.Development.json and whether the dev server for that port supports HTTPS, for example the frontend preset's serveOverHttps setting, before reporting.

rules.statement: In an ASP.NET Core endpoint that calls `HttpRequest.ReadFormAsync`, catch `InvalidDataException` and answer 400 with the endpoint's usual invalid-request error, not a 500.
rules.why: A malformed or oversized form body makes ReadFormAsync throw InvalidDataException. Left uncaught, a client input error becomes a 500 and an error log entry, unlike every other bad input to the endpoint.
rules.check: Look for ReadFormAsync calls that have no try/catch for InvalidDataException mapping to the endpoint's 400 response.

rules.statement: Don't put results from a single run, such as a count of passing tests, in an architecture decision record. State what the decision makes the tests do instead.
rules.why: A count from one run goes out of date as soon as the suite changes.
rules.check: Look in the Consequences sections of ADRs for specific test counts or one-off run results.

rules.statement: In a test project, a new test file declares the same namespace as the sibling test files in its folder.
rules.why: A file with a different namespace from its neighbours is inconsistent with the rest of the project.
rules.check: Compare the namespace declared in a new test file with the namespaces of the other files in the same folder.

rules.statement: Wrap `///` doc comment paragraphs to the usual line width (120 columns), with no awkward line breaks in the middle of a sentence.
rules.why: A paragraph split awkwardly is hard to read.
rules.check: Look for rewritten doc comments that break lines well short of the line width, partway through a phrase.

rules.statement: In Markdown docs, wrap prose to the file's line width and pad table cells to the column widths.
rules.why: Unwrapped prose and misaligned table rows make the source hard to read, and a formatter will rewrap them.
rules.check: Look for edited Markdown lines that break partway through a sentence short of the line width, and table rows whose cells are wider or narrower than their column.

rules.statement: When a test checks the set of keys or entries a configuration produces, assert the exact set, not just that one expected entry is present.
rules.why: A containment assertion lets unexpected entries pass, so the test stops catching stray additions.
rules.check: Look for exact-equality assertions on collections that were loosened to contains-style checks, such as toStrictEqual becoming toContain or Assert.Equal becoming Assert.Contains.

rules.statement: When an endpoint must not build URLs from the request Host header, add an endpoint-level test that sends a forged Host and asserts the published URLs don't change. Configure an issuer that differs from the request host so the assertion means something.
rules.why: Unit tests of the document builder can't catch an endpoint that starts reading Host again, so the Host-spoofing fix could regress with no failing test.
rules.check: For changes that stop deriving origins from the request, check for an integration or endpoint test that sends a spoofed Host header against an explicit issuer and asserts the output URL.
